causes_found: checkpoint retention: when the list of 8 was full, every other task's checkpoint within checkpoint_min_step (32768) of the previous one was erased, which left the first prompt's T-8196 checkpoint (2447 here) and the current task's; a second session on the same system prompt went back to 2447 and processed 8.1K of it again, and editing the second message went back to 0
three sessions started together each computed the same 10.6K prefix: 32K tokens in one batch stream, 34 s for each first answer
a new session took over the slot sharing the most with it and cut that conversation (f_keep 0.69 >= 0.5: not even saved) while a slot was free; nothing was ever copied between slots
with more conversations than slots and no disk tier, least-recently-used eviction under a round-robin pattern keeps evicting the conversation needed next
changes: anchors: checkpoints at the first user message (kept for good), the last one, the end of each prompt (T-4; T-(4+ubatch) only when the last message starts before it), and turn starts spaced by --checkpoint-min-step (now 4096) and a quarter of the distance to the end; a full list drops the checkpoint minimising (gap before x gap after) / distance from the end

a prompt whose best-sharing slot holds another conversation (a quarter or more of it would be cut) takes a free slot, still looks in the RAM and disk tiers, and gets the shared prefix copied in: attention rows device to device (llama_strix_kv_copy_rows), the recurrent state from the source slot's checkpoint
a prompt whose prefix a busy slot is computing waits (deferred) until that slot is past its first or last user message, then copies it; 120 s at most; STRIX_PREFIX_WAIT=0 turns it off
four slots by default (manager DEFAULTS parallel=4)
